proof_nl:
Fix positive integers d and r with gcd(d,r)=1 and r\le d, and fix n>1 with n\equiv 1\pmod{2d}. These arithmetic hypotheses are not needed for the algebraic rewriting, but they are part of the stated setting.

For each k with 0\le k\le n-1, write
S_k(q):=[3dk+r]_q\,(q^r,q^r,q^d;q^{2d})_k\,(q^d;q^d)_k^2\,q^{k(d-dk-2r)/2}\big/(q^{2d};q^{2d})_k.
Then by definition,
T_{d,r,n}(q)=\sum_{k=0}^{n-1} S_k(q).
Also, the exponent k(d-dk-2r)/2 is an integer by the statement, so the monomial q^{k(d-dk-2r)/2} is a well-defined element of \mathbf Q(q).

Now fix such a k. Using the definition (u;q)_k=\prod_{j=0}^{k-1}(1-uq^j), we have
(q^{2d};q^{2d})_k=\prod_{j=0}^{k-1}\bigl(1-q^{2d}(q^{2d})^j\bigr)=\prod_{j=0}^{k-1}\bigl(1-q^{2d(j+1)}\bigr),
(q^d;q^d)_k=\prod_{j=0}^{k-1}\bigl(1-q^d(q^d)^j\bigr)=\prod_{j=0}^{k-1}\bigl(1-q^{d(j+1)}\bigr),
and
(-q^d;q^d)_k=\prod_{j=0}^{k-1}\bigl(1-(-q^d)(q^d)^j\bigr)=\prod_{j=0}^{k-1}\bigl(1+q^{d(j+1)}\bigr).
Therefore
\begin{aligned}
(q^d;q^d)_k(-q^d;q^d)_k
&=\prod_{j=0}^{k-1}\bigl(1-q^{d(j+1)}\bigr)\bigl(1+q^{d(j+1)}\bigr)\\
&=\prod_{j=0}^{k-1}\bigl(1-q^{2d(j+1)}\bigr)\\
&=(q^{2d};q^{2d})_k.
\end{aligned}
This identity is in the polynomial ring \mathbf Q[q], hence also in its fraction field \mathbf Q(q).

Substituting this factorization into S_k(q), we get in \mathbf Q(q)
\begin{aligned}
S_k(q)
&=[3dk+r]_q\,(q^r,q^r,q^d;q^{2d})_k\,(q^d;q^d)_k^2\,q^{k(d-dk-2r)/2}\Big/\Big((q^d;q^d)_k(-q^d;q^d)_k\Big)\\
&=[3dk+r]_q\,(q^r,q^r,q^d;q^{2d})_k\,(q^d;q^d)_k\,q^{k(d-dk-2r)/2}\big/(-q^d;q^d)_k\\
&=A_{d,r,n,k}(q).
\end{aligned}
So each summand of T_{d,r,n}(q) is exactly A_{d,r,n,k}(q).

Summing this equality over k=0,1,\dots,n-1 yields
T_{d,r,n}(q)=\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}A_{d,r,n,k}(q)
inside \mathbf Q(q).

This is precisely the claimed rewriting, equivalently using
(q^{2d};q^{2d})_k=(q^d;q^d)_k(-q^d;q^d)_k
for each k.
solver_summary: Expand the three q-Pochhammer symbols by definition. Their products show termwise that (q^{2d};q^{2d})_k=(q^d;q^d)_k(-q^d;q^d)_k. Substituting this into the kth summand of T_{d,r,n}(q) cancels one factor of (q^d;q^d)_k and gives exactly A_{d,r,n,k}(q). Summing over k proves the identity in Q(q).
vetter_reason: The proof establishes exactly the claimed termwise rewriting in Q(q): it expands the q-Pochhammer products, proves (q^(2d);q^(2d))_k = (q^d;q^d)_k (-q^d;q^d)_k for each k, substitutes this into the original summand, and then sums over k=0,...,n-1. No forbidden or undeclared dependencies are used, and the argument matches the lemma and its role in the assembly.
